summary: This note describes Abuja, the planned capital city of Nigeria, located in the Federal Capital Territory. It was built mainly in the 1980s and replaced Lagos as capital on 12 December 1991. The note highlights its geography, defined by Aso Rock, and nearby Zuma Rock. The source text is duplicated, with two near-identical paragraphs that differ only in how the road to Kaduna is described.
one_line: Abuja is Nigeria's planned capital, built mainly in the 1980s and made capital in 1991, known for Aso Rock and Zuma Rock.
key_facts: Abuja is the capital city of Nigeria and is located in the centre of the country within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
Abuja is a planned city that was built mainly in the 1980s.
Abuja replaced Lagos, the country's most populous city, as the capital on 12 December 1991.
Abuja's geography is defined by Aso Rock, a 400-metre (1,300 ft) monolith left by water erosion.
The Presidential Complex, National Assembly, Supreme Court and much of Abuja extend to the south of Aso Rock.
Zuma Rock is a 792-metre (2,598 ft) monolith.
Zuma Rock lies just north of Abuja on the expressway to Kaduna, according to the first paragraph.
The second paragraph describes Zuma Rock as lying just north of the city on the road to Kaduna State.
The pronunciation of Abuja is given as /əˈbuːdʒə/.
The note contains two nearly identical paragraphs about Abuja, so it appears to be a duplicated copy.
